concept.name: Concentrated liquidity
concept.definition: Concentrated liquidity is the Uniswap v3/v4 mechanism that lets liquidity providers allocate capital to a custom price range instead of uniformly across all prices, so the same capital provides deeper liquidity (and earns more fees) where trading actually occurs.
concept.intuition: Rather than spreading butter thinly from price 0 to infinity, LPs spread it thickly on the slice of the curve where the market actually trades.
concept.mechanics: Price space is partitioned into discrete ticks (~0.01% apart); an LP position is defined by a lower and upper tick and only earns fees while the current price is inside its range. Within a range the pool behaves like a bounded constant-product curve; when price exits the range, the position holds 100% of the cheaper token and earns nothing until price re-enters.
concept.failure_modes: Out-of-range positions earn zero fees and hold entirely the depreciated asset, amplifying impermanent loss versus full-range liquidity; concentrated positions demand active management, and naive 'set and forget' ranges systematically underperform.
concept.misconceptions: Higher capital efficiency is not free yield — it is higher leverage on the same LP risk, so impermanent loss per unit of capital is larger, not smaller. Concentrated liquidity does not eliminate the constant-product math; it bounds where it applies.
concept.example: On Uniswap v2's DAI/USDC pool, only ~0.5% of capital served trades between $0.99 and $1.01; a v3 LP allocating $10,000 entirely to the 0.99–1.01 range earns the same fees on that volume as roughly $2M of v2-style liquidity.
